A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OTiS/OTIS research, retaining the eight-domain pre-training corpus and core pipeline despite substantial retitling and reorganisation. The main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, cardiac regression, forecasting, scaling, ablation, and representation-analysis results, including additional experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original downstream experiments, frozen-encoder evaluations on UEA/UCR, deployment measurements, and component analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Equation 2 changes the stated visible-token decoder input from the encoder feature alone to that feature plus temporal and domain-specific variate embeddings. The tokeniser, 75%/25% masking mixture, MSE-plus-NCC objective, and stated layer/width configurations otherwise remain the same.

E1.justification: v3 substantially expands evaluation to 23 UEA and 121 UCR archive datasets, SleepEDF sleep staging, and Illness and Traffic forecasting. The pre-training corpus is retained. TUEV is retained coverage, having already appeared in v2 Appendix G.2.

E2.justification: v3 adds UniTS and evaluates the previously forecasting-only MOMENT comparator in classification and regression. It adds comparators such as TSLANet, CroSSL, and InvConvNet, replaces the TUEV suite including BIOT/LaBraM with a different EEG suite, and adds TTM, Chronos, Timer-XL, Time-MoE, ROSE, and DTAF to forecasting while removing Autoformer and Time-LLM.

E3.justification: v3 uses five-example class prototypes instead of v2's all-training-sample centroids, and adds weighted k-NN, classification linear probing, and deployment protocols. Reported Epilepsy fine-tuning settings change, including learning rate from 1e-3 to 3e-4. Its forecasting text states 96 observed and 336 predicted points, reversing v2, but Figure 9 still depicts approximately 336 observed and 96 predicted points; the actual forecasting setting is therefore unclear.

E4.justification: v3 adds post-fix probability/masking-ratio experiments and an NCC-weight sweep in Tables 15–16, and replaces representative-task component plots with aggregate ablations in Table 5. It removes v2's EEG-only versus multi-domain pre-training study, quantitative EEG coordinate-alignment analysis, and inter-domain PCA analysis. The sine-wave and scaling analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Five fine-tuning seeds remain standard. v3 adds explicit standard deviations to the main classification/regression tables, specifies five independently sampled support-set episodes with matched seeds across encoders, and reports dual-mask experiments across three pre-training seeds. These extend uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in fine-tuning runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive archive and deployment results, including OTIS five-shot balanced accuracies of 55.7% on UEA and 59.8% on UCR in Table 3. Existing reported results also change, such as Gesture accuracy from 63.61% to 78.0% in v2 Table 2a and v3 Table 1a. Larger-variant benchmark rows and training-strategy results are removed. Forecasting updates cannot confidently be interpreted as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation 2 substantively revises the mathematical specification of decoder inputs. v2's explicit PCA-to-electrode-coordinate alignment construction and its R-squared interpretation in Appendix E.2.1 are removed. The principal loss and masking definitions remain equivalent, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 centres its contribution on generalisable multi-domain pre-training and leading performance on 10 of 15 main benchmarks. v3 centres a 7.1M general-purpose encoder, claims competitiveness across 162 tasks, and introduces quantified memory, energy, latency, and resource-constrained deployment claims. Forecasting becomes an exploratory extension to primarily discriminative features.

C2.justification: v3 explains NCC through structural alignment, mean-collapse, and avoiding noise fitting. It reinterprets the retained scaling evidence as encoder-size saturation requiring further engineering, replacing v2's emphasis on larger corpora potentially benefiting larger models. It strengthens representation interpretations to orthogonal disentanglement and adds an explicit limitation concerning irregularly sampled time series.

D1.justification: New appendices specify frozen-evaluation implementation, logistic-regression tuning, and GPU profiling APIs, precision, warm-up, and timing procedures. v3 adds a hyperparameter-search grid and new-task settings, while removing larger-model fine-tuning tables and some domain-handling explanations. Reported Base pre-training GPU-hours change from 115 to 86. Code and weight access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is rebuilt around general-purpose encoders versus specialised forecasters and inductive bias versus scaling. Previously cited MOMENT becomes a central encoder comparator, while works including UniTS, CBraMod, CSBrain, and newer forecasting models are introduced. Earlier positioning around tokenisation and several EEG foundation-model references is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, methodological explanations, and discussion are extensively rewritten around compact encoders and deployment. Experiments and results become separate sections, and the appendices are substantially reorganised and refocused.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column journal layout, replaces the opening overview with a Pareto-frontier figure, and adds masking/loss illustrations and extensive deployment tables. Classification and regression displays are restructured; several PCA figures disappear or are replaced by similarity matrices. Retained sine-property and scaling plots are relocated, and forecast visualisations expand to eight datasets.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence for reusable frozen features through matched UEA/UCR comparisons and fuller uncertainty reporting. However, its central deployment claims exceed the tested GPU setting, whose description is internally inconsistent: Appendix G specifies batch 1024 on a 48GB GPU, while Table 18 reports 161.8MB/sample for OTIS on Heartbeat, exceeding that capacity under the stated normalisation. Forecasting-window descriptions also conflict, and some earlier mechanistic analyses are lost. These gains and unresolved reliability issues prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
